summary: The note chronicles how Robinson Textiles, a medium-sized North Carolina fabric manufacturer, developed and executed a strategic plan for digital integration between September 2023 and autumn 2024. It covers vision setting, a SWOT assessment, a blueprint covering CRM, ERP, e-commerce and digital marketing, employee engagement, vendor partnerships, phased rollout, and data-driven improvement. The company saw revenue and customer growth but still faces change management and cybersecurity challenges, and it is considering IoT next.
one_line: Robinson Textiles, a North Carolina SME, plans and carries out a year-long digital transformation, gaining growth while facing change management and cybersecurity challenges.
key_facts: Janet Robinson, owner of Robinson Textiles, convened her leadership team on September 4, 2023 to develop a strategic plan for digital integration.
Robinson Textiles is a medium-sized fabric manufacturer based in North Carolina with limited technical expertise on staff.
Ronald Pierce, a digital transformation consultant, led the vision-setting activity and said success needs 'a vision that integrates technology with the company's objectives and goals'.
A SWOT analysis of processes, systems, data management and customer interaction points was conducted in late September and early October 2023.
Jenny Liu was hired as lead IT project manager on October 15, 2023 and described the blueprint as 'a living document'.
The blueprint covered a CRM system, an ERP solution, an e-commerce platform, and a digital marketing strategy.
Janet Robinson held a staff town-hall on November 10, 2023, saying 'It's not just about bringing in new tech; it's about bringing people along with you.'
Robinson Textiles partnered with TechFrontiers and MarketWise, finalizing the partnerships by the end of 2023.
The transformation began on January 3, 2024 with phased rollouts starting with back-office processes; TechFrontiers deployed the ERP system.
MarketWise launched a digital marketing campaign to build Robinson Textiles' online presence around January 2024.
Data from the new systems began flowing in by March 2024, enabling data-driven decisions.
The e-commerce platform launched on April 12, 2024, and customer satisfaction rates were reported rising in early May 2024.
Robinson Textiles began scaling with AI for demand forecasting and marketing automation tools in mid-2024.
After a year, revenue was up and the customer base expanded, but change management and cybersecurity remained challenges.
The company is considering the Internet of Things (IoT) to manage manufacturing equipment and logistics.
